Setup.title: Setup wizard

gate.text: Only someone with access to the server can start setup. Enter the token printed by the installer, or generate a new one on the server with:
gate.tokenHelp: Valid for 1 hour. The browser keeps it only in a secure cookie.
gate.adminExists: An administrator account exists. Sign in as an administrator to continue setup.

language.title: Language
language.help: Default language for setup and the administrator account. You can change it in the panel at any time.

checks.title: System pre-checks
checks.help: Checks the API can verify from its own container: PostgreSQL, Redis, database migrations and the background worker. Operating system, disk and port checks run on the server with "sh scripts/install.sh check".

access.title: Deployment and access address
access.help: The address users will open the panel at. The test checks whether the server can reach itself through this address. Behind NAT a server may not reach its own public address; then the address is saved as unverified.

domain.title: Domain and HTTPS
domain.help: The name the panel will be opened at over HTTPS from the internet. DNS, HTTP reachability and the certificate are tested separately; one passing does not mean the others pass. You can also run without a domain: skip this step and use 127.0.0.1 or an SSH tunnel.

services.title: PostgreSQL and Redis
services.help: The application's database and queue connections. These services run only on the internal Docker network and are never exposed to the internet.

admin.title: Administrator account
admin.help: The first account that manages the panel. After this step the setup token stops working and setup continues only with this account.

vmware.title: ESXi / vCenter connection
vmware.help: The VMware infrastructure the platform will manage virtual servers on. Add a standalone ESXi or a vCenter. vCenter does not replace ESXi; it manages hosts centrally. Do not also add a vCenter-managed host as a standalone ESXi.

discovery.title: Datastore and network discovery
discovery.help: The real hosts, datastores, networks and virtual machines read from the connections.

pools.title: Resource pool and IP plan
pools.help: Capacity and IP ranges to offer for sale or use.

monitoring.title: Monitoring and notifications
monitoring.help: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki and Alertmanager: server and service metrics, logs and alert rules. Optional; the panel starts and stops them on the server itself.

summary.title: Final check and summary
summary.help: Status of each step. Setup cannot finish until required steps are done. Once finished, setup endpoints close; reopening needs "node dist/cli.js recover-setup" on the server.

notAvailable.pools: Resource pools are created in Admin → Catalog; this wizard step comes later.

access.label: Panel address
access.help: Examples: https://panel.example.com or http://127.0.0.1:8080 through an SSH tunnel. Do not add a path, query or user info.

hint.DNS_FAILED: The domain did not resolve. Check that the A record points to the server's public IP and has propagated.
hint.CONNECTION_REFUSED: Connection refused. Check port forwarding, the firewall and the address Caddy listens on (LISTEN_ADDRESS).
hint.TIMEOUT: Timed out. A firewall or NAT may be dropping the connection.
hint.TLS_ERROR: The TLS certificate could not be verified. Do not disable certificate checks; fix the certificate and domain.
hint.WRONG_TARGET: This address answers but is not this installation. DNS or a proxy points to another server.
hint.HTTP_ERROR: The address returned an unexpected HTTP response. A proxy in front may not forward /api to this installation.
hint.LOOPBACK_NOT_VERIFIABLE: 127.0.0.1 and localhost cannot be verified from inside the container. You can save it for use through an SSH tunnel.
hint.UNREACHABLE: The address could not be reached. Check the address and the network path.

monitoring.enable: I will use the monitoring components
monitoring.auto: The panel starts and stops these components on the server itself; no command is needed.
monitoring.running: The monitoring components are already running on this server.
monitoring.startingHelp: Starting monitoring on the server. The components need a minute or two to be ready; this page checks every few seconds.

summary.warnVmware: No VMware connection configured: the platform cannot create or manage virtual servers yet.
summary.warnAccess: The panel address could not be verified from this server. Open it from another device to check.
summary.warnHttps: HTTPS is not configured. Do not expose the panel to the internet; use 127.0.0.1 or an SSH tunnel, or complete the domain step.

checkCodes.NO_HEARTBEAT: No signal in the last 90 seconds
checkCodes.TLS_ERROR: TLS certificate could not be verified
checkCodes.CERT_STAGING: Let's Encrypt test (staging) certificate; browsers do not trust it

domain.label: Domain name
domain.help: Example: panel.example.com. A subdomain is recommended rather than the bare domain.

howto.dnsRecord: At your DNS provider create an A record for this name pointing to the server's public IPv4 address. Add an AAAA record only if the server has working public IPv6. Do not enter a private address (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x); behind NAT enter your router's public address and forward ports 80/443 to this server.
howto.ports: Ports 80 and 443 must reach this server from the internet: Let's Encrypt validates over 80 (HTTP-01) or 443 (TLS-ALPN-01). If another web server uses these ports, use the 'behind-proxy' mode.
howto.apply: Run the command below on the server. Use --acme-staging first while testing so repeated attempts do not hit real certificate rate limits. Once it works, run it again without that option.
howto.test: Then use 'Test connection' to check DNS, HTTP and the certificate separately. Caddy renews the certificate automatically and keeps it in a persistent volume (caddy_data).

domain.behindProxy: To run behind an existing Nginx/Caddy/Traefik use 'sudo sh scripts/install.sh behind-proxy': the panel listens with plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 and your proxy terminates TLS. Details: docs/domain-https.md
domain.aaaaWarning: This name has an AAAA (IPv6) record. If IPv6 does not really work on the server, remove the record; otherwise some visitors and certificate validation will fail.

hint.DNS_FAILED: The name did not resolve. Create the A record and wait for it to propagate (minutes to hours).
hint.NO_ADDRESS_RECORDS: The name exists but has no A record. Add an A record pointing to the server's public IPv4 address.
hint.CONNECTION_REFUSED: Connection refused: nothing listens on that port. Did you run the installer's 'domain' command? A firewall or port forwarding may block 80/443.
hint.TIMEOUT: Timed out: a firewall or NAT may be dropping the connection. Open 80/443 in your cloud provider's firewall.
hint.HTTP_ERROR: Unexpected HTTP response. A proxy or CDN in front may not forward requests to this installation.
hint.TLS_ERROR: The certificate could not be verified (expired, for another name or self-signed). Do not disable certificate checks; check the domain and Caddy logs: docker compose logs proxy
hint.CERT_STAGING: This is a test certificate. If everything works, run the command again without --acme-staging to get a real certificate.
hint.WRONG_TARGET: This name answers but is not this installation. DNS or a proxy in front points to another server.
hint.UNREACHABLE: The address could not be reached.

domain.auto: If your domain’s A record points at this server, check it here. To install the certificate, open Settings → Domain and SSL after setup: the panel gets the Let’s Encrypt certificate on the server itself, applies it and goes back to the old address if anything fails. You can skip this step for now.

remove.title: Remove connection

compat.title: Version compatibility

Catalog.intro: Open existing VMware capacity for sale or use; manage packages, rules, images, IP pools and quotas.

warning.STORAGE_FREE_BELOW_HEADROOM: Real free space on the datastores is below the safety headroom.

form.poolIdentityHelp: The location name customers see when ordering.

sms.useHelp: SMS that are part of a task. To send notifications by SMS, turn on the SMS channel on the Notification rules tab.
sms.useTwoFactorHelp: Users with a verified phone get sign-in codes by SMS.
sms.usePhoneHelp: Users verify their number with an SMS code on My account.
sms.notificationsNote: Notification SMS go only to users who verified their phone.
sms.testHelp: Sends one real SMS with the values in the form (without saving).

payments.noneActive: No payment method is active. Pick a provider below, enter its credentials, check them and activate it.

confidence.community: from open-source integrations; confirm with the provider

payments.label: Name shown to customers
payments.labelHelp: Optional; the provider name is used otherwise.
payments.useModeHelp: Both credential sets are kept; this decides which one payments use.
payments.only3d: checked only by a real 3D Secure payment
payments.liveWarning: Live credentials take real payments. Enter the values from the provider’s production merchant panel.
payments.testHelp: Test (sandbox) credentials: payments here never move money. Use the provider’s test panel and test cards.
payments.fillTest: Fill in the public test account
payments.fillTestHelp: Published by the provider or its integrators; may change.
payments.endpointHelp: Leave empty to use the address shown. Only if the provider gave you a different one.

payments.checkNone: This provider has no request that can check credentials without starting a payment. Verify them with a test payment.

checkExplain.rejected: The provider refused them; see its message.
checkExplain.inconclusive: The provider answered, but not in a way that proves the credentials. Read its message.

checkExplain.unverifiable: No online check exists for this provider.

charges.iyzico: Hosted checkout with 3D Secure; saved cards renew automatically if your iyzico account allows non-3D charges.
charges.paytr: Hosted iFrame with 3D Secure. Saved-card renewals need PayTR’s card storage (direct API), so customers pay renewals on the page.

charges.param: Hosted payment page (Ortak Ödeme) with 3D Secure; no saved cards. Your server’s IP must be allowed by Param. News reports place Param under a TMSF trustee since July 2026.
charges.none: Credentials can be saved and checked; taking invoice payments with this provider is not built yet.
charges.paytrUrl: Set this as the notification URL (Bildirim URL) in the PayTR panel

providers.powerdns: Also PowerDNS-Admin setups: the panel talks to PowerDNS directly.

rdns.apiUrlHelp: The PowerDNS webserver, for example http://10.0.0.53:8081 (api=yes, webserver-allow-from must include this server)
rdns.ttlHelp: Seconds the records may be cached
rdns.defaultsHelp: New servers get this PTR on all their addresses. Deleting a server removes its records.
rdns.templateHelp: Variables: {ip}, {ipDashed}, {name}. Empty: new servers get no PTR.
rdns.customerEdit: Customers may change the PTR of their addresses
rdns.forwardCheck: Only names that resolve back to the address (forward-confirmed)
rdns.forwardHelp: The forward check stops customers from naming an address after a domain they do not control. Staff are not checked.
rdns.noZones: No reverse zones on this server. Create the zones of your blocks first (for example 113.0.203.in-addr.arpa).

security.requireHelp: The chosen accounts see only the setup screen until they set it up; the API refuses every other request too.

levelHelp.none: Users turn it on if they want.

security.selfWarning: Two-factor is off on your own account: after saving, you are sent to the setup screen too.
security.methods: Methods: authenticator app (TOTP), one-time codes by SMS or e-mail, backup codes; 10 wrong codes lock verification for 15 minutes. Users can trust a device for 30 days.
security.emailCodeHelp: The sign-in screen offers "Sign in with an e-mail code": no password, a 6-digit code by e-mail. Accounts with two-factor still use password + second step.
security.emailCodeOn: Allow sign-in with an e-mail code
security.needsMail: E-mail (SMTP) is not set up or is off for two-factor codes; the option does not appear on the sign-in screen.
security.apiTokensHelp: Who may create personal API tokens for scripts. Existing tokens keep working until they are removed or expire.

domain.currentHelp: The domain the panel is served on and the certificate it presents.
domain.noDomain: The panel is not served on a domain (local, or behind another proxy).
domain.noCertificate: The certificate could not be read (the proxy may not be answering).

modeHelp.acme: Free, obtained automatically and renewed before it expires. Ports 80 and 443 must be open from outside.
modeHelp.staging: To test without hitting rate limits; browsers do not trust it.
modeHelp.custom: A corporate or paid certificate: full chain and private key (PEM). You renew it.

domain.changeHelp: The new name's A record must point to this server's public IP. The agent on the server applies the change; on failure the previous address is restored.
domain.agentMissingTitle: The server agent is not installed
domain.agentMissing: To change the domain from the panel, run once on the server:
domain.newDomainHelp: The name only: panel.example.com (no scheme or path).
domain.noARecord: This name has no A record; add one pointing to this server's IP at your DNS provider.
domain.sameServer: The name points to the same server as the current address.
domain.otherServer: The name points elsewhere; without NAT or a load balancer no certificate can be obtained.
domain.cannotCompare: No current domain to compare with; make sure the A record points to this server.
domain.certificateHelp: How the HTTPS certificate is provided.
domain.certPemHelp: The server certificate first, then the intermediates (fullchain.pem).
domain.keyPemHelp: An unencrypted private key. Only root reads it on the server; the panel does not keep or show it.
domain.certOk: The certificate and key match ({chain}-certificate chain, {key} key).

warnings.SELF_SIGNED: Self-signed certificate: browsers show a warning.
warnings.CHAIN_INCOMPLETE: Intermediate certificates seem to be missing; some clients may refuse the connection. Use fullchain.pem.
warnings.CHAIN_ORDER: The chain order looks wrong (server certificate first, then intermediates).
warnings.EXPIRES_SOON: The certificate expires in less than 30 days.

confirm.c1: The proxy restarts with the new name; connections may drop for a few seconds.
confirm.c2: The panel is served only on {domain}; the old address stops working.
confirm.c3: Sessions are tied to the address: sign in again at the new one.
confirm.c4: If no certificate can be obtained or verified, the previous settings are restored automatically.

domain.rolledBack: The previous address and certificate were restored; details in the log below.
domain.mayDisconnect: When it completes this page may stop answering on the old address; open https://{domain}.

actionHelp.console: The VM screen in the browser.
actionHelp.iso: Insert images from the location's ISO library.
actionHelp.rootPassword: See the password set or generated at order time.

actionHelp.snapshots: Take, restore and remove snapshots (at most 5 per server).
actionHelp.resize: Customers change vCPU, memory and disk themselves; increases are invoiced for the rest of the period.
actionHelp.reinstall: Customers reinstall from another image (erases the disk).
actionHelp.backups: Customers take, restore and remove backups (on the location's backup storage).

servers.rolesNote: Other rights, such as managing firewalls, are set on the Roles page.
servers.hardwareHelp: Applies to VMs created from now on; existing ones do not change.

hwHelp.cpuHotAdd: vCPUs can be added while the server runs (the guest OS must support it).
hwHelp.memoryHotAdd: RAM can be added while the server runs.
hwHelp.nestedHv: Hardware virtualization inside the guest (KVM, Hyper-V, Docker Desktop). Always on for ESXi images.

servers.hardwareNote: Hot add affects some licensing and NUMA settings; measure performance on large VMs.
servers.trafficHelp: What happens when a server has used all of its monthly traffic (customers are warned at 80% and 100% either way).
servers.overLimitThrottle: Limit the speed until it is covered again
servers.throttleHelp: In and out, on the server's distributed switch ports. Lifted at the start of the month or after a bigger package.
servers.backupsHelp: Customers take and restore backups of their own servers.
servers.deleteHelp: A deleted server is shut down and can be taken back during this time; then it is deleted for good. 0: deleted at once.

announcement.notLive: Saved, but not shown right now: it is outside its time window.

chat.telegramTokenHelp: Checked with Telegram when saved. The bot must not have a webhook set.

chat.pushoverHelp: Create an application on pushover.net and enter its API token; users add their own user keys.

statusPage.title: Status page
statusPage.help: The public /status page: the state of components and locations and the live announcement. No connection names or customer data are shown.

directory.title: Sign in with LDAP / Active Directory
directory.intro: People sign in with their company directory e-mail and password; their accounts and roles come from the directory.
directory.howItWorks: People type their e-mail and password on the sign-in form. Directory accounts (and people with no account yet) are checked against the directory; local panel accounts (such as the first administrator) keep signing in with their own password. Two-factor and role limits apply to directory users too. Directory passwords cannot be changed or reset in the panel.
directory.connectionHelp: The directory server and the service account used to find people.
directory.urlHelp: ldaps://server:636 (recommended) or ldap://server:389 with StartTLS. Plain ldap:// sends passwords in clear text.
directory.startTlsHelp: Encrypts an ldap:// connection. Not needed with ldaps://.
directory.caPemHelp: If the directory's certificate comes from a company CA, that CA's certificate. The certificate is always checked.
directory.bindDnHelp: A read-only account. In AD, user@domain.com works too. Empty: anonymous search.
directory.peopleHelp: Where and how people are looked up.
directory.userFilterHelp: {email} is replaced with the e-mail from the sign-in form (safely escaped). Examples in the guide.
directory.autoCreate: Create the account on first sign-in
directory.autoCreateHelp: Off: only directory accounts already created in the panel can sign in.
directory.rolesHelp: Roles given by group membership. With mappings, roles follow the directory at every sign-in; without, the panel's roles stay.
directory.testHelp: With the values in the form (not saved), the service account binds. With an e-mail, that person is looked up; with their password too, their sign-in is tried. No account is created.
directory.testSignedIn: Person found and their password accepted.
directory.ssoIntro: Let people sign in with your organization’s identity provider: Keycloak, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, Authentik, Zitadel or any OpenID Connect provider.
directory.ssoUsers: {n, plural, one {# account signs in with single sign-on} other {# accounts sign in with single sign-on}}.
directory.ssoHow: The panel asks the provider who the person is (code flow with PKCE; the ID token’s signature is checked with the provider’s keys). New people get an account, and their roles follow the groups below. An e-mail address that already belongs to a panel or directory account is never taken over by the provider. Their password and second factor stay at the provider.
directory.ssoNameHelp: Shown on the sign-in page as “Sign in with …”.
directory.issuerHelp: The provider’s issuer; the panel reads {issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration. https only.
directory.redirect: Redirect URI to register at the provider
directory.scopesHelp: Must include openid. Add the scope that puts groups in the token if your provider needs one (for example “groups”).
directory.groupsClaimHelp: The claim that lists the person’s groups (groups, roles, …).
directory.ssoGroup: Group name as the provider sends it
directory.ssoAutoCreateHelp: Off: only people who already signed in with single sign-on can come in.

incidents.newHelp: Announce a problem or planned maintenance: it shows on the public status page and, while open, at the top of every panel page.
incidents.title: Title
incidents.messageHelp: Say what happened and what is being done; customers see this.
incidents.removeBody: The incident and all its updates are removed from the status page.

support.departmentsHelp: The departments customers pick when they open a ticket. A switched-off department is hidden for new tickets; tickets of a removed one are kept.

signIn.title: Ways to sign in
signIn.intro: The password and passkeys are always available. Turn on more ways here; each one follows the same rules (bans, role address limits, captcha, rate limits).
signIn.guards: Directory (LDAP) and single sign-on accounts keep signing in where their password lives. A provider that reports an existing address never takes over that account: people link providers themselves from Account → Security.
signIn.socialHelp: Sign in with an account people already have. Register this panel at the provider, paste its client ID and secret, and give the provider the redirect URI shown.
signIn.socialSignUp: Let new people create an account with these providers
signIn.socialSignUpHelp: Only while registration is open. Off: providers sign in existing accounts that linked them.
signIn.tenantHelp: common (any account), organizations (work or school only), consumers, or your tenant ID / domain.
signIn.hostedDomainHelp: Optional: only accounts of this domain (* for any Workspace domain).
signIn.redirect: Redirect URI to register at the provider
signIn.oneTapHelp: Shows Google’s one-tap sign-in prompt on the sign-in page. Add {origin} to “Authorized JavaScript origins” of the Google client.
signIn.passwordlessHelp: A one-time link by e-mail, or a user name instead of the e-mail address.
signIn.magicLinkHelp: A link valid for 10 minutes, once. Only for existing panel accounts; needs working e-mail.
signIn.needsMail: E-mail is not set up: links cannot be sent until it is (Settings → E-mail).
signIn.username: Sign in with a user name
signIn.usernameHelp: People choose a user name in Account → Profile and can then sign in with it instead of the e-mail address (panel passwords only).
signIn.checks: Checks on new accounts and passwords
signIn.checksHelp: Run when an account is created or a password is set.
signIn.pwned: Refuse passwords found in data breaches
signIn.pwnedHelp: Checked with Have I Been Pwned: only the first 5 characters of the password’s SHA-1 hash leave the server. If the service cannot be reached, the password is accepted.
signIn.disposableHelp: Sign-ups from disposable e-mail domains (a list of 55,000+ domains) are refused.

billing.enabledHelp: Orders and renewals are invoiced and collected. Existing servers get a subscription on their monthly anniversary.
billing.requirePaymentHelp: A new server is built only after its first invoice is paid (or covered by balance).
billing.autoChargeHelp: Renewals are paid from the balance, then the default saved card, without the customer.
billing.balanceHelp: Customers can top up and pay invoices from their balance.

billing.companyHelp: Printed on every invoice and sent in the e-invoice. Required before billing is turned on.
billing.websiteHelp: e-Arşiv internet sales need the address of the site.
billing.taxHelp: KDV on hosting is 20% unless your accountant says otherwise.
billing.pricesIncludeTaxHelp: Catalog prices are what the customer pays; KDV is taken out of them.
billing.exportExemptHelp: Service export (exemption 302). Turn on only if your accountant confirms it for your services.
billing.collectionHelp: When renewals are invoiced, reminders sent and unpaid services held.
billing.timeline: What happens to an unpaid renewal
billing.balanceAndTransferHelp: Top-up limits, and the account customers can transfer to.
billing.bankTransferHelp: Shown on unpaid invoices; you record the payment when it arrives.
billing.testingHelp: Try the whole flow without a real provider.
billing.sandboxHelp: Customers can pay with test cards (4242 4242 4242 4242). Never on with real customers.
billing.hourlyHelp: Customers may order hourly servers paid from their balance (needs the balance). Each month's use becomes one invoice.
billing.hourlyMinHours: Hours the balance must cover to order
billing.hourlyMinHoursHelp: For example 24: a day of the server's price.

einvoice.integratorHelp: The GİB-approved private integrator that signs and delivers your invoices. Paid invoices go there by themselves.
einvoice.unverified: Built from its published documentation; try one invoice in test first
einvoice.sandboxHelp: Issues nothing at GİB. For trying the flow: tax numbers ending in an even digit act as e-Fatura users.
einvoice.noneHelp: Invoices are numbered and shown in the panel; no e-invoice is issued. Choose an integrator before taking real money.
einvoice.secretKept: Saved; leave empty to keep it
einvoice.endpointHelp: Only if your integrator gave you a different address.
einvoice.testFailed: The integrator did not accept the account.
einvoice.numberingHelp: GİB numbers: 3 characters, the year, 9 digits; each series counts on its own, without gaps.
einvoice.profileHelp: Basic suits hosting; with commercial the buyer may reject within 8 days.
einvoice.senderAliasHelp: Your e-Fatura sender label from the integrator; some need it.
einvoice.rule1: A buyer registered for e-Fatura gets an e-Fatura in its inbox; everyone else an e-Arşiv invoice by e-mail.
einvoice.rule2: Registration is checked again at every invoice, since buyers join the list every day.

einvoice.rule4: A refund within 8 days cancels an e-Arşiv invoice; later, or for e-Fatura, you are told a return invoice is due.

Firewalls.title: Firewalls
Firewalls.intro: Rule sets you attach to your servers. Everything coming in that no rule allows is dropped; outgoing traffic is open unless you add outbound rules. VMware enforces the rules on the virtual switch, so they work whatever runs inside the server.
Firewalls.emptyBody: Create one from a template (for example a web server: SSH, HTTP, HTTPS and ping) and attach it to your servers.
Firewalls.name: Name
Firewalls.templateHelp: You can change every rule afterwards.

templateDesc.empty: No rules: nothing reaches the server until you add some.
templateDesc.web: SSH, HTTP, HTTPS and ping from anywhere.
templateDesc.windows: Remote Desktop and ping from anywhere.

Firewalls.applyHelp: A server can have up to {n} firewalls; their rules add up.
Firewalls.removeBody: The firewall and its rules are deleted.
Firewalls.removeInUse: It is still attached to {n, plural, one {# server} other {# servers}}. Detach it first.
Firewalls.howBody: Inbound: only what a rule allows gets in (replies to connections the server opens itself are always allowed). Outbound: everything is allowed until you add an outbound rule; then only what the rules allow goes out. Changes are applied to all attached servers within seconds.
Firewalls.inboundHelp: Traffic to your server. Sources: which addresses may connect.
Firewalls.outboundHelp: Traffic from your server. Leave empty to allow all outgoing traffic.
Firewalls.noInbound: No inbound rules: all incoming traffic is blocked.
Firewalls.noOutbound: No outbound rules: all outgoing traffic is allowed.
Firewalls.ipsHelp: addresses or networks, separated by commas
Firewalls.serversHelp: Servers protected by this firewall (at most {n} firewalls per server).
Firewalls.pendingHelp: means the new rules are being written to VMware.
Firewalls.serverOpen: No firewall: every port of this server is reachable.
Firewalls.serverNone: No firewall is attached. Attach one from the Firewalls page.
Firewalls.orderHelp: Optional. Applied before the server first starts.

Updates.title: Updates
Updates.intro: Check for new versions and update from here. The server runs the same update as the command line: a backup first, running tasks paused, the new version started and checked, and an automatic rollback if it does not come up.
Updates.agentMissingTitle: The update agent is not installed on this server
Updates.agentMissing: The panel cannot run anything on the host by itself. Install the agent once (new installs have it):

channelHelp.edge: Every change on the branch; for test servers.

Updates.availableHelp: Takes a few minutes. The panel restarts and may not answer for a short while.

confirm.step1: An encrypted backup is taken first; nothing changes if it fails.
confirm.step2: Running server tasks are paused and continue afterwards from their last step.
confirm.step3: The new version is built and started; the panel is unavailable for a few minutes.
confirm.step4: If it does not become ready, the previous version is started again automatically.
confirm.step5: Database changes are not undone automatically; the backup can restore them.

action.terminal: Turning the terminal on or off

Updates.restarting: The panel is restarting with the new version. This page keeps trying and continues on its own.
Updates.failed: The task failed ({code}). The log below says why; with a failed update the previous version is running again.
Updates.switchHelp: Moves to this version with the same safety steps. Going back to an older version is refused when the database was already changed by a newer one.
Updates.autoHelp: The hourly maintenance timer installs new versions of the channel inside the window (server time), and postpones while server tasks are running.
Updates.noTimer: The hourly maintenance timer is off, so nothing runs automatically. Turn it on with:

Topology.title: Topology
Topology.introAdmin: The live structure from the Internet to locations, clusters, hosts and servers. Packets flow with the real traffic; host bars show CPU and memory use. Refreshed every 15 seconds.
Topology.intro: Where your servers run and their traffic. A shield on a link means a firewall is applied.
Topology.motionOff: Packet animation is off because motion is reduced.
Topology.refresh: Data is refreshed from VMware every 15 seconds; traffic is the average of the last 20 seconds.

Energy.title: Power and energy
Energy.measuring: Measurement requested; it updates in a few seconds.
Energy.intro: Current host power, kWh, cost and carbon. Hosts with a power counter are measured, the others estimated from a profile and CPU use; each server gets a share of its host's power by CPU use. Sampled every 5 minutes.
Energy.measuredOf: {measured} of {hosts} hosts measure power directly; the others are estimated.
Energy.noData: No measurements yet. Start with "Measure now".
Energy.rangeTotal: Range total: {kwh} kWh · {cost} · {co2} kg CO₂ (PUE included)
Energy.hostsHelp: For hosts without a power counter, enter idle and full-load watts to improve the estimate (from the vendor's power calculator or a measurement).
Energy.profileHelp: The estimate is linear between idle and full load by CPU use.
Energy.profileSaved: Profile saved; used from the next measurement.
Energy.noLocations: No pools are assigned to a location.
Energy.serversHelp: The top 50 servers, from their host's power shared by CPU use.
Energy.settingsHelp: For cost and carbon. PUE accounts for cooling and facility load.
Energy.co2Help: Carbon intensity of the grid (about 420 for Turkey).

Abuse.title: Abuse monitoring
Abuse.scanFailed: The request could not be sent.
Abuse.intro: Risky ports open to the Internet on customer servers (databases, Redis, SMB, Docker API…) and CPU at full load for hours (a cryptocurrency-mining suspicion). A finding stays open while the condition lasts.
Abuse.noneResolved: Nothing closed in the last 7 days.
Abuse.ackHelp: The finding stays open but is not reported again. Note why it is accepted.
Abuse.disclaimer: A CPU finding is a signal, not proof: builds, rendering or scientific work look the same. Look into it before contacting the customer.
Abuse.settingsHelp: The port scan tries a TCP connection to every server IPv4 address; the CPU check uses the 5-minute energy samples.
Abuse.portsHelp: One per line: port and label, e.g. "6379 Redis".
Abuse.notifyCustomer: Also notify the customer about an open port
Abuse.cpuHelp: Suspicious when at least 90% of the samples in this window are above the threshold.

Vdc.title: Virtual datacenters
Vdc.explain: Give a customer a fixed allocation (vCPU, RAM, disk, server count) in a pool for a monthly price. It is reserved in the pool at once; the customer creates servers of any shape within it, which carry no price of their own and do not count against the user quota.

Guides.open: What is it, how to set it up?
Guides.disclaimer: This guide follows the services' official documentation. Services change their interfaces; if a step does not match, check the current documentation linked above.

powerdns.title: Reverse DNS (PTR) with PowerDNS
powerdns.intro: Reverse DNS tells which name an IP address belongs to (e.g. 192.0.2.10 → web1.example.com). Many mail servers distrust mail from IPs without a PTR record. The panel writes PTR records through the HTTP API of a PowerDNS Authoritative server that hosts the reverse zones of your IP blocks: new servers get the default name, customers may change theirs, a deleted server's record is removed.

sections.title: Prerequisite: the reverse zone is delegated to you
sections.text: PTR records are visible on the Internet only when the block's reverse zone (2.0.192.in-addr.arpa for 192.0.2.0/24) is delegated to your name servers. If the block is registered to you (an LIR in the RIPE region), create a "domain" object in the RIPE Database with at least two nserver entries; RIPE checks your name servers on submission and the delegation can take up to 24 hours to appear. If you rent the block from a data centre or provider, ask them for the delegation.
sections.note: The panel works with whole zones: IPv4 blocks of /24 and larger, and ip6.arpa zones for IPv6. RFC 2317 classless delegation (CNAMEs, used for blocks smaller than /24) is not supported yet.

sections.title: Install PowerDNS (Ubuntu / Debian)
sections.text: A server separate from the panel is recommended. Delegation needs at least two name servers (one can be a secondary). The distribution package is enough; repo.powerdns.com has newer versions.
sections.code: sudo apt install pdns-server pdns-backend-sqlite3 sqlite3
sections.note: PowerDNS will not start if another service (e.g. systemd-resolved) uses port 53; check with "sudo ss -lunp | grep :53".

sections.title: Create the database (SQLite)
sections.text: SQLite is enough for small and medium setups; large ones can use the PostgreSQL backend (pdns-backend-pgsql).
sections.code:
sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/powerdns
sudo sqlite3 /var/lib/powerdns/pdns.sqlite3 < /usr/share/doc/pdns-backend-sqlite3/schema.sqlite3.sql
sudo chown -R pdns:pdns /var/lib/powerdns

sections.title: Turn on the API: /etc/powerdns/pdns.conf
sections.text: Remove other launch= lines (e.g. in files under /etc/powerdns/pdns.d/), then add the following. Generate the key with "openssl rand -hex 32".
sections.code:
launch=gsqlite3
gsqlite3-database=/var/lib/powerdns/pdns.sqlite3
api=yes
api-key=A-LONG-RANDOM-KEY
webserver=yes
webserver-address=0.0.0.0
webserver-port=8081
webserver-allow-from=PANEL_SERVER_IP/32

# then:
sudo systemctl restart pdns
sections.note: Never expose the API to the Internet: webserver-allow-from must list only the panel's IP, and the firewall should open port 8081 to the panel only.

sections.title: Create the reverse zone
sections.text: The zone name is the first three octets in reverse: 192.0.2.0/24 → 2.0.192.in-addr.arpa. ns1.example.com is your name server.
sections.code:
# PowerDNS 4.x (the Ubuntu 24.04 package):
sudo -u pdns pdnsutil create-zone 2.0.192.in-addr.arpa ns1.example.com

# PowerDNS 5.0 and later:
sudo -u pdns pdnsutil zone create 2.0.192.in-addr.arpa ns1.example.com

sections.title: In the panel
steps: Provider: PowerDNS.
API URL: http://DNS_SERVER:8081 (no path; the panel adds /api/v1/...).
API key: the api-key from pdns.conf.
Server ID: localhost (the PowerDNS default).
Default PTR template, e.g. {ipDashed}.customers.example.com.
Test: the reverse zones found are listed. Then Save.

telegram.title: Telegram bot
telegram.intro: The panel sends notifications through a Telegram bot you create. Creating a bot is free and takes a few minutes.

sections.title: Create the bot
steps: Open a chat with @BotFather in Telegram (Telegram's official, verified account).
Send /newbot.
Give the bot a display name (e.g. "Lightning VM Notifications").
Give it a username ending in "bot" (e.g. lightningvm_alerts_bot).
BotFather replies with a token like 123456789:AA…; copy it.
sections.note: The token is full control of the bot; keep it secret. If it leaks, use /revoke in BotFather and enter the new token in the panel.

sections.title: Appearance (optional)
sections.text: In BotFather, /setuserpic sets a picture and /setdescription the text users see when they first open the bot.

sections.title: In the panel
steps: Settings → Messaging → tick Telegram.
Paste the token and Save. The panel checks it with Telegram and shows the bot's name.

sections.title: Important: no webhook on the bot
sections.text: The panel reads pairings with getUpdates. If another application set a webhook on the bot, Telegram refuses that call. Use the bot for this panel only, or remove the webhook:

sections.title: How users connect
sections.text: Account → Notifications → Connect an app → Telegram. The panel opens a one-time link; the user presses Start in Telegram, then "Verify connection" in the panel. The link is valid for 15 minutes.

whatsapp.title: WhatsApp Business (Cloud API)
whatsapp.intro: Notifications are sent with Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API from a number your business owns. Because the business starts the conversation, Meta requires an approved message template. Template messages may be charged at Meta's current prices.

sections.title: What you need
steps: A Meta business account (business.facebook.com).
A phone number for the business. If it is registered in the WhatsApp app, delete it there first.
A payment method in Meta for template messages.

sections.title: Create the app
steps: developers.facebook.com → My Apps → Create App; pick the WhatsApp / business use case.
Add the WhatsApp product and connect your business account.
On WhatsApp → API Setup, add and verify your number and copy its "Phone number ID".
sections.note: The test number on API Setup can only message recipients you add there; add your own number for real use.

sections.title: Permanent access token
steps: business.facebook.com → Business settings → Users → System users → Add.
Assign your app and WhatsApp account to the system user with full control.
"Generate token": pick the app; tick whatsapp_business_messaging and whatsapp_business_management.
The token is shown once; copy it right away.
sections.note: The temporary token on API Setup expires quickly; enter the permanent one in the panel.

sections.title: Message template
steps: WhatsApp Manager → Message templates → Create template.
Category: Utility (transactional notification).
Name: lowercase letters, digits and underscores (e.g. panel_notification). Language: English (en_US) or another.
Put two variables in the body: the panel fills {{1}} with the title and {{2}} with the text.
Submit for review; use it once its status is "Active".
sections.note: Meta does not allow the body to start or end with a variable; keep fixed text before and after the variables.

sections.title: In the panel
steps: Settings → Messaging → tick WhatsApp.
Enter the permanent token, Phone number ID, template name and the template's language code (e.g. en_US or tr), then Save.
Users connect with the verified phone number on their account.

links.label: Meta: WhatsApp Cloud API get started

pushover.title: Pushover
pushover.intro: Pushover is a push notification service for iOS, Android and desktop. You create an application token; each user has their own Pushover account and app (a one-time purchase per platform after the trial).

sections.title: Application token
steps: Sign up and sign in at pushover.net.
Under "Your Applications", choose "Create an Application/API Token".
Name it (e.g. Lightning VM), accept the terms and create it.
Enter the 30-character API Token/Key in Settings → Messaging → Pushover.

sections.title: Users
sections.text: Each user enters their own User Key, shown on the pushover.net home page after signing in, in Account → Notifications → Connect an app → Pushover.

captcha.title: Bot protection (CAPTCHA) keys
captcha.intro: Protects sign-up, sign-in and password reset forms from automated attacks. All three providers have free use. Each gives a site key (sent to the browser) and a secret key (kept on the server).

sections.title: Cloudflare Turnstile
steps: dash.cloudflare.com → Turnstile → Add widget. Your domain does not have to be on Cloudflare.
Name the widget and add the panel's hostname.
"Managed" mode is recommended.
Copy the Site Key and Secret Key.

sections.title: Google reCAPTCHA
steps: Go to google.com/recaptcha/admin/create.
Type: v2 "I'm not a robot" checkbox, or v3 (invisible, scored).
Add the panel's domain and copy the site key and secret key.
sections.note: v3 scores each request from 0.0 (bot) to 1.0 (human); requests below the panel's minimum score are refused. The type chosen in the panel must match the key's type.

sections.title: hCaptcha
steps: dashboard.hcaptcha.com → Sites → New Site; add the panel's domain and copy the Sitekey.
The secret is account-wide: Account Settings → Secret Keys.

sections.title: Test
sections.text: Use Test on Settings → Bot protection before saving. If the domain is not in the provider's list, the request is refused.

mail.title: Sending e-mail
mail.intro: The panel sends e-mail for password resets, two-factor codes and notifications. Use your own SMTP server or an e-mail service's API.

sections.title: SMTP or API?
sections.text: SMTP works with any mail server. API providers (Resend, SendGrid, Amazon SES…) send over HTTPS and are not affected by the SMTP ports many cloud providers block.

sections.title: SMTP settings
steps: 587 with STARTTLS is the most common; 465 uses TLS directly.
Gmail / Google Workspace: with two-step verification on, create an "App password" and use it as the password.
Microsoft 365: SMTP sending must be allowed for the mailbox; Microsoft is restricting basic authentication, so check its current documentation or choose an API provider.
The sender address must be one the signed-in account may send as.

sections.title: Domain authentication: SPF, DKIM, DMARC
sections.text: To stay out of spam, add the records your provider gives you to the sending domain's DNS:
steps: SPF: a TXT record listing who may send for you (e.g. v=spf1 include:provider-host ~all). One SPF record per domain.
DKIM: the signing record your provider gives (TXT or CNAME).
DMARC: a TXT record on _dmarc. To start with:
sections.note: Gmail and Yahoo require SPF, DKIM and DMARC from bulk senders; adding all three helps delivery even at low volume.

sections.title: Test
sections.text: Use Test on the E-mail tab to send a real message before saving; the error tells you where the problem is.

domain.title: Domain and HTTPS
domain.intro: The panel gets a free Let's Encrypt certificate for your domain and renews it before it expires.

sections.title: DNS record
steps: Add an A record in your domain's DNS: e.g. panel.example.com → the server's IPv4 address.
If the server has a working IPv6 address, add an AAAA record too. A wrong AAAA record breaks certificate validation; leave it out if unsure.
Wait for it to propagate (usually minutes; depends on the record's TTL).

sections.title: Ports
sections.text: Ports 80 and 443 must be open from the Internet to the server: in your cloud provider's security group and in the server's firewall. Let's Encrypt validates over these ports.

sections.title: Using Cloudflare
sections.text: Setting the record to "DNS only" (grey cloud) while the first certificate is issued avoids problems; turn the proxy on afterwards. With the proxy on, choose SSL/TLS mode "Full (strict)".

sections.title: In the panel
sections.text: Enter the domain and press Check: DNS, HTTP and the certificate are checked one by one. Save when all pass.
sections.note: Let's Encrypt limits certificates and failed attempts per domain; many attempts in a row can lead to a temporary block. Check DNS and ports first.

vmware.title: ESXi / vCenter connection
vmware.intro: The panel connects to VMware with a service account, reads the inventory and creates servers through vCenter. Creating servers needs vCenter; on a standalone ESXi the inventory, console and metrics work.

sections.title: Service account
steps: vSphere Client → Administration → Single Sign On → Users and Groups → new user in vsphere.local (e.g. lightning).
Give it a strong password. vsphere.local passwords expire under the default password policy; an expired password breaks the connection, so check the policy.
sections.note: In vCenter 9, accounts using identity federation cannot sign in with a password; use a vsphere.local or LDAP/AD account.

sections.title: Role and privileges
sections.text: Administration → Access Control → Roles → create a role with these privileges (discovery checks them; actions that depend on a missing one show as "not supported"):
sections.code:
System.View, System.Read
VirtualMachine.Inventory.Create, VirtualMachine.Inventory.Delete
VirtualMachine.Interact.PowerOn, .PowerOff, .Reset, .ConsoleInteract
VirtualMachine.Config.CPUCount, .Memory, .AddNewDisk
VirtualMachine.Provisioning.Clone
VirtualMachine.State.CreateSnapshot, .RevertToSnapshot, .RemoveSnapshot
Datastore.AllocateSpace, Network.Assign, Resource.AssignVMToPool

sections.title: Assign the permission
steps: In Hosts and Clusters, right-click the vCenter root → Add Permission.
Pick the user and the role; keep "Propagate to children" ticked.

sections.title: Template
sections.text: Servers are cloned from a VM template. The template needs cloud-init (with VMware Tools / open-vm-tools); the panel sets the network, hostname and SSH keys through it.

sections.title: TLS
sections.text: If vCenter's certificate is not from a trusted CA (such as the default VMCA certificate), the connection test shows its subject, issuer and SHA-256 fingerprint. Compare the fingerprint with the one in vSphere Client or on the server, then pin it. Validation is never switched off.

ldap.title: Sign in with LDAP / Active Directory
ldap.intro: The panel checks people against your company directory (Active Directory, OpenLDAP, FreeIPA…). A read-only service account first finds the person by e-mail, then the panel binds as them with their own password. The directory checks the password; the panel keeps no clear-text password.

sections.title: Network and encryption
steps: The panel server must reach the directory on port 636 (LDAPS) or 389 (LDAP + StartTLS).
ldaps:// is recommended. If the directory's certificate comes from a company CA, paste that CA's certificate into "Root certificate".
sections.note: Do not use plain ldap://: passwords would cross the network in clear text.

sections.title: Service account
sections.text: Create a read-only account whose password does not expire. In Active Directory, the bind DN can be the full DN or the UPN (svc-lightning@example.com).

sections.title: Active Directory
sections.text: Search base: DC=example,DC=com. This filter leaves out disabled accounts. Attributes: mail, displayName, memberOf.

sections.title: OpenLDAP
sections.text: Search base: ou=people,dc=example,dc=com. The name attribute is usually cn. memberOf needs the memberof overlay on the server.

sections.title: FreeIPA
sections.text: Search base: cn=users,cn=accounts,dc=example,dc=com. Attributes: mail, displayName, memberOf.

sections.title: Roles
sections.text: In a group mapping, enter the group's full DN (e.g. CN=Panel Admins,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com) and pick the roles it gives. Someone in several groups gets all their roles; someone in none gets the default role.

sections.title: Try it
steps: In Test, run it empty: the service account should bind.
Enter an e-mail: the person's DN, groups and roles appear.
Enter their password too: their sign-in is checked. Then save and turn it on.
sections.note: Local accounts such as the first administrator are not affected by the directory; if the directory is unreachable, sign in with one of them.

oidc.title: Single sign-on with OpenID Connect
oidc.intro: People sign in with your organization’s identity provider instead of a panel password. The panel registers as a “client” (an application) at the provider; the provider confirms who the person is and, if you want, which groups they are in.

sections.title: What every provider needs
steps: Create a web application (a confidential client) using the authorization code flow.
Register the redirect URI shown on this page exactly, including https and the panel’s domain.
Copy the client ID and client secret into the panel.
Enter the issuer URL: the panel adds /.well-known/openid-configuration itself.
sections.note: The panel must be reachable over https at the address in the redirect URI, and it must be able to reach the provider.

sections.title: Keycloak
sections.text: Clients → Create client → OpenID Connect. Turn on Client authentication and the Standard flow, and add the redirect URI under Valid redirect URIs. The secret is on the Credentials tab. For groups, add a “Group membership” mapper to the client (or a client scope it uses) with Token Claim Name groups and Full group path off.

sections.title: Microsoft Entra ID
sections.text: App registrations → New registration, platform Web, with the redirect URI. Create a secret under Certificates & secrets. For groups, use Token configuration → Add groups claim; Entra then sends the groups’ object IDs, so map those IDs to roles here.

sections.title: Okta
sections.text: Applications → Create App Integration → OIDC, Web Application, with the redirect URI as a sign-in redirect URI. For groups, in the app’s Sign On tab edit the OpenID Connect ID Token section: groups claim type Filter, claim name groups, a regex such as .* (with a custom authorization server, add the claim there instead).

sections.title: Google Workspace
sections.text: Google Cloud console → APIs & Services → Credentials → Create OAuth client ID, type Web application, with the redirect URI. Google sends no groups: everyone gets the default role.

sections.title: authentik
sections.text: Create an OAuth2/OpenID provider (confidential client) with the redirect URI, and an application that uses it. The issuer ends with the application’s slug.

sections.title: Roles and safety
steps: Press “Check the provider”: the panel reads the discovery document and lists the claims the provider offers.
Map each group name (exactly as the provider sends it) to roles; someone in no mapped group gets the default role.
An e-mail address that already belongs to a panel or directory account is refused: the provider cannot take over that account.
Passwords and second factors are managed at the provider; the panel does not ask these people for its own two-factor.
sections.note: Keep at least one local administrator account: it still signs in with its password if the provider is down.

links.label: Okta: Customize tokens with a groups claim

social.title: Social sign-in (Google, Microsoft, GitHub…)
social.intro: Each provider needs this panel registered as an application (an OAuth client). You give the provider the redirect URI shown under the provider in Settings; the provider gives you a client ID and a client secret.

sections.title: For every provider
steps: The panel must be served over https on its final address: the redirect URI contains it.
Copy the redirect URI from the provider card exactly (…/api/auth/callback/<provider>).
Paste the client ID and secret, turn the provider on and save. The secret is stored encrypted and never shown again.
sections.note: Existing panel accounts are never taken over by a provider: people link a provider themselves in Account → Security. New accounts through providers only when you allow it and registration is open.

sections.title: Google
sections.text: Google Cloud console → APIs & Services: set up the OAuth consent screen, then Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID, type “Web application”. Add the redirect URI under “Authorized redirect URIs”. For One Tap, also add the panel address under “Authorized JavaScript origins”. Requested scopes: openid, email, profile.

sections.title: Microsoft (Entra ID)
sections.text: Microsoft Entra admin center → App registrations → New registration; platform “Web” with the redirect URI. Certificates & secrets → New client secret: copy its Value (not the Secret ID). Tenant: “common” for any Microsoft account, “organizations” for work or school accounts only, or your Directory (tenant) ID from the app’s Overview.

sections.title: GitHub
sections.text: GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App. Homepage URL: the panel address; Authorization callback URL: the redirect URI. Then “Generate a new client secret”. Requested scopes: read:user, user:email.

sections.title: GitLab
sections.text: GitLab → User settings (or a group’s / the instance’s admin area) → Applications → Add new application, with the redirect URI and the read_user scope; keep it confidential.

sections.title: Discord
sections.text: Discord Developer Portal → Applications → New Application → OAuth2: copy the client ID, reset to get the client secret, and add the redirect URI under Redirects. Requested scopes: identify, email.

sections.title: Facebook
sections.text: Meta for Developers → My Apps → Create app, add the “Facebook Login” product, and add the redirect URI under Facebook Login → Settings → Valid OAuth Redirect URIs. App ID and App secret (App settings → Basic) are the client ID and secret. Requested permissions: email, public_profile.

sections.title: LinkedIn
sections.text: LinkedIn Developers → Create app, then on Products request “Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect”. On the Auth tab add the redirect URI under Authorized redirect URLs; the Client ID and Primary Client Secret are shown there. Requested scopes: openid, profile, email.

Support.queueIntro: Late tickets first, then those whose deadline is closest. Deadlines follow the priority.
Support.cannedVars: Placeholders: {a} (the customer), {b} (the ticket number), {c} (its server). They are filled in when you pick the reply.

Support.presenceTyping: {who} is writing a reply — check before you answer.

HostSettings.intro: The machine the panel runs on: its name, clock and time zone, time servers and DNS servers. Changes are applied by the host agent, which checks them again.
HostSettings.refreshQueued: The agent will record the current details
HostSettings.agentMissingTitle: The host agent is not installed

HostSettings.noDetails: No details recorded yet: press “Refresh details”.

HostSettings.driftBehind: {s, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} behind your computer

HostSettings.pending: {n, plural, one {# change} other {# changes}} not applied yet

Billing.title: Billing
Billing.intro: Invoices, subscriptions, your balance and saved cards. An invoice is issued as soon as it is paid.
Billing.off: Billing is not turned on in this panel.
Billing.profileMissingHelp: Invoices go to your account name until you add your identity or tax number and address.

kpi.openCount: {n, plural, one {# invoice} other {# invoices}}{overdue, plural, =0 {} other {, # overdue}}
kpi.autoCharge: Paid automatically from balance or saved card

topup.title: Top up your balance
topup.help: Your balance pays invoices automatically. A top-up is not a sale, so it has no invoice of its own; the invoices it pays do.

Billing.noSubscriptions: No subscriptions yet: each server you order becomes one.
Billing.autoRenewOff: It will not renew; you get no new invoice for it.
Billing.cancelTitle: Cancel at the end of the period?
Billing.cancelBody: {name} keeps running until {date}, then it is deleted with its data. Nothing more is charged.
Billing.cancelled: It ends at the end of the period.
Billing.cardsHelp: Cards you chose to save at payment. Only the payment provider holds the card; the panel keeps its last four digits. The default card pays invoices automatically.
Billing.noCards: No saved card. Tick "save the card" when you pay.
Billing.defaultSet: This card pays invoices automatically now.

profile.whoHelp: A person invoices with their T.C. identity number, a company with its tax number and tax office.
profile.countryHelp: Two-letter code, e.g. TR, DE, GB.
profile.einvoiceUser: This tax number is registered for e-Fatura: your invoices arrive in your e-invoice inbox.
profile.addressHelp: As it should appear on the invoice.
profile.emailHelp: e-Arşiv invoices are e-mailed here; empty uses your account e-mail.
profile.appliesTo: Applies to unpaid and future invoices; issued ones stay as they are.

sheet.label: Invoice
sheet.exemption: KDV exemption code {code} (KDV Law 11/1-a, service export).

decline.PROVIDER_ERROR: The payment provider did not answer.

Billing.failedToast: The payment did not go through. The invoice still awaits payment.
Billing.checkingHelp: The provider is confirming it; this page updates by itself.
Billing.orderWaits: Your server is set up as soon as this is paid.
Billing.withCardHelp: You finish the payment on the provider’s secure page with 3D Secure; the panel never sees the card.
Billing.saveCard: Save the card for automatic payments
Billing.saveCardHelp: The provider keeps it; renewals are then paid without you.
Billing.transferHelp: Send the amount to this account; the invoice is marked paid when it arrives.
Billing.noMethod: No payment method is available yet. Please contact support.

hourly.title: Pay as you go
hourly.help: Hourly servers are paid from the balance; each month's use becomes one invoice.

BillingAdmin.title: Billing
BillingAdmin.intro: Recurring revenue, open and overdue invoices, collected money, every invoice, subscription and payment.
BillingAdmin.payments: {n, plural, one {# payment} other {# payments}} this month
BillingAdmin.off: Orders are not invoiced and nothing is collected until billing is turned on.
BillingAdmin.sandbox: Customers can pay with test cards. Turn it off before taking real money.
BillingAdmin.search: Number, name, e-mail or tax number

done.suspend: Suspended: the server is shut down and held.

BillingAdmin.invoiceCreated: Invoice created; the customer was told.
BillingAdmin.adjustHelp: A goodwill credit or a correction. Positive adds to the balance, negative takes away; the reason is kept in the history.
BillingAdmin.editHelp: A server’s renewal uses its current price; the next renewal invoice follows the period end you set.
BillingAdmin.withdrawBody: It disappears from what the customer owes. Nothing was paid on it.
BillingAdmin.markPaidHelp: For money that arrived outside the panel: {amount} is recorded and the invoice issued.
BillingAdmin.refundHelp: Up to {amount}. By default it goes back to the card through the provider.
BillingAdmin.toBalance: Refund to the customer’s balance instead
BillingAdmin.recorded: Payment recorded; the invoice is issued.

ServerChange.started: Resize started; the server restarts with its new size.
ServerChange.startedInvoice: Resize started. An invoice for the difference is in Billing.

resize.title: Change size
resize.help: More or fewer vCPUs and memory, or a bigger disk. The server is shut down cleanly, changed and started again (about a minute).
resize.diskGrowOnly: A disk can only grow (now {gb} GB). The file system grows on the next boot.
resize.nothingNow: Nothing; the new price applies from the next period
resize.offline: The server is off and stays off.
resize.shrinkNote: Less memory or fewer CPUs: check that what runs on it still fits.

reinstall.title: Reinstall
reinstall.help: A fresh install from an image. Addresses, firewalls, the price and the server name stay; everything on the disk is erased.
reinstall.keysHelp: Otherwise the keys the server has now are put on the new install.
reinstall.warning: All data on the server is erased, including its snapshots. This cannot be undone.
reinstall.started: Reinstall started; the server is rebuilt from the image.
reinstall.locked: The server is locked; unlock it to reinstall.

Developer.copyNow: Copy it now: it is shown only once

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.help: For scripts and tools: a token acts as you, with your permissions. Read-only tokens can only look; full tokens can also change things. Tokens cannot open consoles or manage tokens.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.usage: Send it as "Authorization: Bearer <token>" to /api/… on this panel.
tokens.removeBody: Scripts that use it stop working at once.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.help: Your notifications (server ready, invoice paid, …) also sent as signed JSON to your HTTPS address. Failed deliveries are retried for a few hours.
webhooks.urlHelp: A public HTTPS address; private networks are refused.
webhooks.allHelp: Everything you are notified about, now and later.
webhooks.failing: {n, plural, one {# failure} other {# failures}} in a row
webhooks.offHelp: Switched off after many failed deliveries. Save it again to switch it on.
webhooks.rotateBody: The old secret stops working at once; update your receiver with the new one.
webhooks.secretHelp: Your receiver checks each request with it: the X-Lightning-Signature header holds t=<time>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "time.body">.
webhooks.verifyHelp: Compute the HMAC over the raw body exactly as received, compare in constant time and refuse old timestamps.

usage.title: Using the API
usage.help: Every action of the panel is an API call. State changes on servers need an Idempotency-Key header, so a retry never runs twice.
usage.docs: The full reference is in docs/api.md of the installation.

Traffic.title: Traffic
Traffic.help: Network traffic in and out, counted from VMware every few minutes.
Traffic.notYet: Not counted yet; the first figures appear a few minutes after the server runs.
Traffic.throttledHelp: This month's traffic is used up, so the speed is limited until the month ends. A bigger package lifts it within minutes.

Import.title: VMs to import
Import.help: VMs in vCenter that the panel did not create. Importing one gives it to a customer as a server: it keeps running, is renamed to the panel's name for it, and from then on is managed like any server (power, console, snapshots, billing). Its address is recorded from the location's IP pools.
Import.noPool: This vCenter has no location (resource pool) yet; add one in Catalog first.
Import.emptyHelp: Every VM here is a template or already the panel's. Refresh the inventory on the VMware page to see new ones.
Import.name: Server name
Import.imageHelp: Used if the server is reinstalled later.
Import.addressHelp: Optional; must be free in this location's IP pools.

Disputes.title: Dispute #{number}
Disputes.noneHelp: If an invoice looks wrong, open it and choose "Dispute this invoice".
Disputes.formHelp: Tell us what is wrong. Our billing team answers in the conversation and decides; while the dispute is open the invoice is not collected.

reason.tax_details: Wrong invoice details (tax ID, name, address)

reasonHelp.wrong_amount: The price or the period is not what was agreed.
reasonHelp.not_used: Billed for something you did not use.
reasonHelp.duplicate: The same thing appears on two invoices.
reasonHelp.service_problem: An outage or a fault during the period.
reasonHelp.tax_details: The invoice needs other buyer details.

Disputes.amountHelp: Empty: the chosen lines, or the whole invoice. At most {max}.
Disputes.messageHelp: What happened and what you expect. You can add screenshots or documents.
Disputes.paused: While the dispute is open, no reminders, automatic charges or suspension happen for this invoice.
Disputes.withdrawBody: The invoice is collected as usual again.

remedyHelp.balance: Usable for any invoice; refunds a paid one into the balance.
remedyHelp.cancel: The unpaid invoice is withdrawn completely.

Disputes.inReview: Taken into review; the customer was told
Disputes.noteHelp: Sent in the conversation and shown on the invoice.
Disputes.decided: Decision saved; the customer was told

Backups.title: Backups
Backups.help: A copy of the disk on separate backup storage, taken while the server runs. Restoring one replaces everything on the disk.
Backups.notConfigured: Backups are not set up for this location yet.
Backups.restoreWarning: The server is shut down, its disk is replaced with this backup, and it starts again if it was running. Everything written after the backup is lost.
Backups.started: Backup started; it is ready in a few minutes.
Backups.full: The limit is reached: remove an older backup first.

Reseller.title: Reseller
Reseller.intro: Your customers and their servers. Servers are billed to you at a {discount}% discount; what you charge your customers is up to you.
Reseller.monthly: All servers together: {amount} a month (after your discount).
Reseller.customersHelp: A new customer gets an account; they set their password with "Forgot password" on the sign-in page. You can see and manage their servers.
Reseller.name: Name
Reseller.sshKeyHelp: Added to the customer's keys and put on the server.

admin.title: Reseller
admin.help: A reseller opens customer accounts and orders servers for them within this allocation; their servers are billed to the reseller at the discount. Empty: no limit.
admin.using: Using now: {servers} servers, {vcpu} vCPU, {memory} GB, {disk} GB disk.
admin.stopped: No longer a reseller; their customers are ordinary accounts now

Reseller.notReseller: This account is not a reseller. Ask us if you would like to resell servers.
Reseller.brandHelp: Your customers see this name and colour in the panel instead of ours.
Reseller.brandNote: Empty name: your customers see the panel as it is. You see your brand too.

Placement.title: Placement
Placement.help: Staff only: move the server to another host or datastore while it keeps running (vMotion). Placement is from the last inventory refresh.

Disks.title: Extra disks
Disks.help: More disks beside the system disk, added while the server runs. A new disk is empty: partition and mount it in the server.
Disks.notSold: This location does not sell extra disks.
Disks.removeBody: Everything on it is deleted. Unmount it in the server first.

Networks.title: Private networks
Networks.intro: Networks of your own between your servers in a location, isolated from everyone else (a VLAN of their own). Traffic on them is not counted.
Networks.name: Name
Networks.subnetHelp: A private range such as 10.10.0.0/24; empty: one is chosen.
Networks.noneHelp: Create one, then add servers of the same location.
Networks.noLocations: No location offers private networks yet.
Networks.leaveTitle: Take this server off the network?
Networks.leaveBody: Its interface on this network is removed.
Networks.removeBody: Only an empty network can be deleted.
Networks.setupHelp: The new interface has MAC {mac}. On Linux with netplan:

Images.title: Save as an image
Images.help: Your own image of this server's disk as it is now, to order new servers or reinstall from. Only you see it. For a clean copy of databases, shut the server down first.
Images.name: Image name
Images.saving: The image is being made; it appears in the order page when it is ready.
Images.mineHelp: Images you saved from your servers. Order a server from one on the order page.
Images.none: No images yet. Save one from a server's page.
Images.servers: {n, plural, =0 {not in use} one {# server uses it} other {# servers use it}}
Images.removeBody: Its copy in vCenter is deleted. Servers made from it keep running.
Images.full: You have the most images you can keep; delete one first.

Coupons.title: Coupons
Coupons.newHelp: Customers enter the code when ordering a monthly server. It takes the amount off the first invoices, or all of them.
Coupons.periodsHelp: Empty: every invoice. 1: the first one only.
Coupons.noteHelp: Only staff see it (a campaign, a partner).
Coupons.newCustomers: Only for customers with no server yet
Coupons.packagesHelp: None chosen: every package and custom sizes.
Coupons.subscriptions: {n, plural, one {# subscription discounted} other {# subscriptions discounted}}
Coupons.deleteBody: Nobody has used it yet; it goes away for good.

Transfers.title: Hand over to another account
Transfers.help: The server, its subscription, snapshots and backups move to the account you name once it accepts. The offer stays open for 7 days.
Transfers.staffHelp: Moves the server and its subscription to the account at once; both owners are told.
Transfers.keeps: The root password and SSH keys inside the server stay as they are: the new owner should change them.
Transfers.offerBody: {email} can accept it within 7 days. Until then the server stays yours.
Transfers.moveBody: It belongs to {email} from now on, with its subscription.
Transfers.incomingHelp: Accepting makes the server yours; its invoices come to you from the next one.
Transfers.outgoingHelp: Offers you made in the last 30 days.
Transfers.noneIn: Nobody has offered you a server.
Transfers.noneOut: You have not offered a server.
Transfers.acceptBody: It becomes yours with its subscription: {price} a month from the next invoice.
